title: Evaluation and Testing Pipelines
summary: This day covers essential concepts for building AI engineering skills.
content:
# Evaluation and Testing Pipelines ##### The prompt change that shipped on a Friday A team in Pune improved their RAG system prompt. It was clearly better — more concise answers, fewer hedges, cleaner citations. They tested it on six queries, all good, and merged. Monday brought complaints. The new prompt had dropped one clause from the old version: *"If the context does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I could not find this in the documents."* Without it the model fabricated. Refusal rate went from 7% to 0.4% — which looked like an improvement on the dashboard — while hallucination rate went from 3% to 19%. Nobody noticed for four days because there was no automated evaluation, and the metric that moved was one they were not watching. An evaluation gate in CI would have caught it in ninety seconds. They had the eval set; they had never wired it to the pipeline. **An evaluation you run manually is an evaluation you will skip under deadline pressure.** Day 16 covered what to measure; today is the machinery that makes measurement automatic, blocking, and continuous. ##### The evaluation stack ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Code / prompt change"] --> B["CI: unit tests
seconds"] B --> C["CI: golden dataset evals
2-5 min, BLOCKING"] C --> D{"Regression?"} D -->|Yes| E["Block merge"] D -->|No| F["Merge → staging"] F --> G["Nightly: full eval suite
30-60 min"] G --> H["Canary: 1% traffic"] H --> I["Online metrics
+ guardrails"] I --> J{"Healthy?"} J -->|No| K["Auto rollback"] J -->|Yes| L["Progressive rollout"] L --> M["Production monitoring"] M --> N["Failures → eval set"] N --> C ``` | Layer | When | Duration | Blocking | Purpose | |---|---|---|---|---| | Unit tests | Every commit | < 30s | Yes | Logic correctness | | **Golden evals** | **Every PR** | **2–5 min** | **Yes** | **Catch regressions** | | Full suite | Nightly | 30–60 min | No | Comprehensive coverage | | Canary | On deploy | Hours | Auto-rollback | Real traffic validation | | Online monitoring | Continuous | — | Alerts | Drift and degradation | **The golden-eval layer is the one that matters most and is most often missing.** It must be fast enough that nobody is tempted to skip it — under five minutes — which constrains how large it can be. ##### Offline versus online **Offline** evaluation runs against a fixed dataset with known answers. Reproducible, fast, and blind to real-world distribution. **Online** evaluation measures production traffic. Real distribution, but no ground truth and slow feedback. You need both, and they answer different questions: ```python from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Callable, Optional, Literal @dataclass class EvalCase: id: str category: str question: str context: Optional[str] = None reference_answer: Optional[str] = None expected_chunk_ids: Optional[set] = None must_contain: Optional[list[str]] = None must_not_contain: Optional[list[str]] = None should_refuse: bool = False difficulty: Literal["easy", "medium", "hard"] = "medium" tags: list[str] = None GOLDEN_SET = [ EvalCase( id="refuse-001", category="unanswerable", difficulty="medium", question="Does the contract cover services in Sri Lanka?", context="Clause 2: Services shall be provided within India.", should_refuse=True, must_not_contain=["Sri Lanka is covered", "yes, it covers"], tags=["hallucination_guard"], ), EvalCase( id="extract-014", category="extraction", difficulty="easy", question="What is the notice period for terminating the MSA?", context="Clause 8.1: Either party may terminate by providing ninety (90) " "days written notice.", reference_answer="90 days written notice, per Clause 8.1.", must_contain=["90", "8.1"], expected_chunk_ids={"msa-2026::c14"}, ), ] ``` **The `should_refuse` cases are the ones that would have caught the Pune bug.** A golden set without unanswerable questions cannot detect a lost refusal instruction, and refusal cases are the single highest-value category to include. ##### The three-layer evaluator Run cheap deterministic checks first; escalate only what passes. ```python from dataclasses import dataclass import json import re @dataclass class CheckResult: name: str passed: bool detail: str = "" layer: str = "rule" class LayeredEvaluator: """Rule checks → reference metrics → LLM judge.""" REFUSAL_MARKERS = ["could not find", "not covered", "not specified", "does not contain", "unable to determine"] def __init__(self, judge_fn=None, judge_threshold=3.5): self.judge_fn = judge_fn self.judge_threshold = judge_threshold def rule_checks(self, case: EvalCase, answer: str, retrieved_ids: list = None) -> list[CheckResult]: out = [] if case.must_contain: missing = [s for s in case.must_contain if s.lower() not in answer.lower()] out.append(CheckResult("must_contain", not missing, f"missing: {missing}" if missing else "")) if case.must_not_contain: present = [s for s in case.must_not_contain if s.lower() in answer.lower()] out.append(CheckResult("must_not_contain", not present, f"forbidden present: {present}" if present else "")) refused = any(m in answer.lower() for m in self.REFUSAL_MARKERS) out.append(CheckResult("refusal_behaviour", refused == case.should_refuse, f"refused={refused}, expected={case.should_refuse}")) if case.context: ans_nums = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\.?\d*\b", answer.replace(",", ""))) ctx_nums = set(re.findall(r"\b\d[\d,]*\.?\d*\b", case.context.replace(",", ""))) invented = ans_nums - ctx_nums - {"1", "2", "3"} out.append(CheckResult("numbers_grounded", not invented, f"invented: {invented}" if invented else "")) if case.expected_chunk_ids and retrieved_ids is not None: hit = set(retrieved_ids) & case.expected_chunk_ids out.append(CheckResult( "retrieval_hit", bool(hit), f"retrieved {len(hit)}/{len(case.expected_chunk_ids)} expected")) return out def evaluate(self, case: EvalCase, result: dict) -> dict: answer = result.get("answer", "") checks = self.rule_checks(case, answer, result.get("retrieved_ids")) rule_passed = all(c.passed for c in checks) judge_scores = None # Only invoke the judge if the cheap checks passed if rule_passed and self.judge_fn and not case.should_refuse: judge_scores = self.judge_fn(case, answer) overall = rule_passed and ( judge_scores is None or min(judge_scores.values()) >= self.judge_threshold) return { "case_id": case.id, "category": case.category, "passed": overall, "rule_checks": [{"name": c.name, "passed": c.passed, "detail": c.detail} for c in checks], "judge_scores": judge_scores, "failed_checks": [c.name for c in checks if not c.passed], } ``` **Rule checks run in microseconds and catch the highest-severity failures.** The `numbers_grounded` and `refusal_behaviour` checks together would have blocked the Pune merge, and neither requires an LLM call. ##### RAG-specific metrics RAGAS decomposes quality into retrieval and generation, which is what tells you where to fix. ```python from datasets import Dataset from ragas import evaluate as ragas_evaluate from ragas.metrics import (faithfulness, answer_relevancy, context_precision, context_recall, answer_correctness) def run_ragas(cases: list[EvalCase], system_fn, metrics=None): """Build the RAGAS dataset from your golden set and score it.""" metrics = metrics or [faithfulness, answer_relevancy, context_precision, context_recall] data = {"question": [], "answer": [], "contexts": [], "ground_truth": []} for case in cases: result = system_fn(case.question) data["question"].append(case.question) data["answer"].append(result["answer"]) data["contexts"].append([c["text"] for c in result["chunks"]]) data["ground_truth"].append(case.reference_answer or "") scores = ragas_evaluate(Dataset.from_dict(data), metrics=metrics) return scores def interpret_ragas(scores: dict) -> list[str]: """Turn four numbers into a diagnosis.""" findings = [] recall = scores.get("context_recall", 1.0) precision = scores.get("context_precision", 1.0) faith = scores.get("faithfulness", 1.0) relevancy = scores.get("answer_relevancy", 1.0) if recall < 0.75: findings.append( "RETRIEVAL bottleneck: relevant chunks are not being retrieved. " "Fix chunking, add hybrid search, or improve the embedding model.") if precision < 0.60 and recall >= 0.75: findings.append( "RETRIEVAL precision low: too much irrelevant context. " "Add or tune the reranker; reduce top_k.") if faith < 0.85 and recall >= 0.75: findings.append( "GENERATION bottleneck: the model is not grounding in the context. " "Strengthen the prompt, lower temperature, or reduce context size.") if relevancy < 0.80: findings.append( "Answers are not addressing the question. Check prompt clarity.") if not findings: findings.append("No dominant bottleneck; improvements will be incremental.") return findings ``` **Reading recall against faithfulness is the diagnostic that matters.** High faithfulness with low recall means fix retrieval; the reverse means fix the prompt. Optimising the wrong one is how teams spend five weeks on chunk size, as in Day 19. ##### Agent trajectory evaluation Agents need a different approach: the final answer can be right for the wrong reasons, or wrong because of one bad step in an otherwise sound trajectory. ```python from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass class TrajectoryCase: id: str task: str expected_tools: set[str] forbidden_tools: set[str] max_steps: int max_cost_inr: float success_check: Callable[[str], bool] def evaluate_trajectory(case: TrajectoryCase, result: dict) -> dict: """Score the path, not just the destination.""" trace = result.get("trace", []) tools_used = {t["tool"] for t in trace if t.get("tool")} checks = { "task_succeeded": case.success_check(result.get("answer", "")), "used_required_tools": case.expected_tools.issubset(tools_used), "avoided_forbidden": not (case.forbidden_tools & tools_used), "within_step_budget": len(trace) <= case.max_steps, "within_cost_budget": result.get("cost_inr", 0) <= case.max_cost_inr, "no_repeated_failures": _max_consecutive_same_tool(trace) <= 2, } return { "case_id": case.id, "passed": all(checks.values()), "checks": checks, "steps_used": len(trace), "cost_inr": round(result.get("cost_inr", 0), 3), "tools_used": sorted(tools_used), "efficiency": round(len(case.expected_tools) / max(len(trace), 1), 2), } def _max_consecutive_same_tool(trace) -> int: """Detect an agent stuck retrying the same failing tool.""" if not trace: return 0 best = run = 1 for a, b in zip(trace, trace[1:]): run = run + 1 if a.get("tool") == b.get("tool") else 1 best = max(best, run) return best ``` **`no_repeated_failures` catches the most common agent pathology** — the loop where a tool fails and the agent retries it identically, which Day 26's budgets bound but do not prevent. **Efficiency matters as much as success.** An agent solving a task in fourteen steps when three suffice is expensive and slow, and that shows up in the trajectory but never in the final answer. ##### LLM-as-judge in a pipeline ```python import json from openai import OpenAI from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor client = OpenAI() JUDGE_PROMPT = """Evaluate the answer against the rubric. QUESTION: {question} CONTEXT PROVIDED: {context} REFERENCE ANSWER: {reference} ANSWER TO EVALUATE: {answer} Score 1-5 with a one-sentence justification: correctness — 5: matches the reference/context exactly 3: partially correct 1: wrong groundedness — 5: every claim traceable to the context 3: one unsupported inference 1: fabricated specifics completeness — 5: covers everything the context supports 3: covers the main point, misses detail 1: substantially incomplete conciseness — 5: no padding or unnecessary hedging 3: some filler 1: verbose Return ONLY JSON: {{"correctness": {{"score": N, "why": "..."}}, "groundedness": {{"score": N, "why": "..."}}, "completeness": {{"score": N, "why": "..."}}, "conciseness": {{"score": N, "why": "..."}}}}""" def judge_case(case: EvalCase, answer: str, model="gpt-4o") -> dict: r = client.chat.completions.create( model=model, temperature=0.0, response_format={"type": "json_object"}, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": JUDGE_PROMPT.format( question=case.question, context=(case.context or "(none)")[:3000], reference=case.reference_answer or "(none)", answer=answer)}], ) parsed = json.loads(r.choices[0].message.content) return {k: v["score"] for k, v in parsed.items()} def judge_batch(pairs, model="gpt-4o", max_workers=8): """Parallel judging — sequential is the bottleneck in CI.""" with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool: return list(pool.map(lambda p: judge_case(p[0], p[1], model), pairs)) ``` **Concrete score anchors are what make a judge reliable.** "5: every claim traceable to the context" produces consistent scoring; "rate the groundedness" produces everything clustered at 4. **Calibrate before trusting it**, exactly as Day 16 argued: ```python def calibrate_judge(judge_fn, human_labelled, min_spearman=0.75): import numpy as np from scipy.stats import spearmanr j = [judge_fn(r["case"], r["answer"])["correctness"] for r in human_labelled] h = [r["human_score"] for r in human_labelled] rho, p = spearmanr(j, h) return { "spearman": round(float(rho), 3), "p_value": round(float(p), 5), "exact_agreement": round(float(np.mean(np.array(j) == np.array(h))), 3), "within_one": round(float(np.mean(np.abs(np.array(j) - np.array(h)) <= 1)), 3), "usable": rho >= min_spearman, } ``` **Recalibrate whenever you change the judge model or the rubric.** A judge validated six months ago against a rubric that has since been edited is not validated. ##### The regression gate The Pune fix. This is the artefact that turns evaluation into a safety net. ```python import json from pathlib import Path from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass class RegressionThresholds: """Per-metric tolerance. Some metrics must never regress at all.""" overall_pass_rate: float = 0.02 # allow 2 pp drop hallucination_guard: float = 0.0 # ZERO tolerance refusal_behaviour: float = 0.0 # ZERO tolerance faithfulness: float = 0.03 context_recall: float = 0.05 p95_latency_pct: float = 0.20 # allow 20% slower cost_per_query_pct: float = 0.15 class RegressionGate: def __init__(self, baseline_path="eval/baseline.json", thresholds: RegressionThresholds = None): self.baseline_path = Path(baseline_path) self.thresholds = thresholds or RegressionThresholds() self.baseline = (json.loads(self.baseline_path.read_text()) if self.baseline_path.exists() else None) def check(self, current: dict) -> dict: if self.baseline is None: self.save_baseline(current) return {"status": "baseline_created", "blocked": False} regressions, improvements = [], [] for metric, tolerance in vars(self.thresholds).items(): key = metric.replace("_pct", "") if key not in current or key not in self.baseline: continue base, now = self.baseline[key], current[key] higher_is_better = key not in ("p95_latency", "cost_per_query") if metric.endswith("_pct"): delta = (now - base) / max(base, 1e-9) bad = delta > tolerance else: delta = now - base bad = (base - now) > tolerance if higher_is_better else delta > tolerance entry = {"metric": key, "baseline": round(base, 4), "current": round(now, 4), "delta": round(delta, 4), "tolerance": tolerance} if bad: regressions.append(entry) elif (higher_is_better and delta > 0) or (not higher_is_better and delta < 0): improvements.append(entry) # Per-category zero-tolerance check for cat, base_rate in self.baseline.get("by_category", {}).items(): now_rate = current.get("by_category", {}).get(cat, 0) if cat in ("unanswerable", "hallucination_guard") and now_rate < base_rate: regressions.append({"metric": f"category:{cat}", "baseline": base_rate, "current": now_rate, "delta": now_rate - base_rate, "tolerance": 0.0}) return { "status": "regression" if regressions else "ok", "blocked": bool(regressions), "regressions": regressions, "improvements": improvements, } def save_baseline(self, results: dict): self.baseline_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) self.baseline_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2)) ``` **Zero tolerance on hallucination guards and refusal behaviour.** Those are safety properties, not quality metrics, and a 2% regression in refusal correctness is not an acceptable trade for a 3% gain in conciseness. **Guardrail metrics on latency and cost** prevent a quality win that triples your bill from shipping unnoticed. ##### Wiring it into CI ```yaml # .github/workflows/eval.yml name: Evaluation on: pull_request: paths: ["app/**", "prompts/**", "config/**", "eval/**"] jobs: golden-evals: runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 15 steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-python@v5 with: python-version: "3.11" cache: pip - run: pip install -e ".[eval]" - name: Restore eval cache uses: actions/cache@v4 with: path: .eval_cache key: eval-${{ hashFiles('eval/golden_set.jsonl') }} - name: Run golden evaluations env: OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }} EVAL_MODE: ci run: python -m eval.run --set golden --output eval/results.json - name: Regression gate run: python -m eval.gate --results eval/results.json --baseline eval/baseline.json - name: Comment results on PR if: always() uses: actions/github-script@v7 with: script: | const fs = require('fs'); const r = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('eval/results.json')); const g = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('eval/gate_result.json')); const rows = g.regressions.map(x => `| ⚠️ ${x.metric} | ${x.baseline} | ${x.current} | ${x.delta} |`).join('\n'); const body = [ `### Evaluation results`, ``, `**Pass rate:** ${(r.overall_pass_rate * 100).toFixed(1)}% ` + `(${r.n_passed}/${r.n_cases})`, `**Faithfulness:** ${r.faithfulness?.toFixed(3) ?? 'n/a'}`, `**p95 latency:** ${r.p95_latency?.toFixed(2)}s`, `**Cost/query:** ₹${r.cost_per_query?.toFixed(4)}`, ``, g.blocked ? `### ❌ Regressions detected\n\n| Metric | Baseline | Current | Δ |\n|---|---|---|---|\n${rows}` : `### ✅ No regressions`, ].join('\n'); github.rest.issues.createComment({ issue_number: context.issue.number, owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, body }); full-suite: if: github.event_name == 'schedule' runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 90 steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: pip install -e ".[eval]" - run: python -m eval.run --set full --output eval/full_results.json - run: python -m eval.report --results eval/full_results.json --slack ``` **Commenting results on the PR is what drives adoption.** A gate that silently blocks is resented; one that explains what regressed and by how much gets fixed. **Caching matters for CI cost.** Deterministic cases at `temperature=0` can be cached by input hash, so unchanged cases skip the API call entirely: ```python import hashlib from pathlib import Path class EvalCache: """Cache deterministic eval results by (case, system fingerprint).""" def __init__(self, cache_dir=".eval_cache"): self.dir = Path(cache_dir) self.dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True) def _key(self, case_id: str, fingerprint: str) -> Path: h = hashlib.sha256(f"{case_id}:{fingerprint}".encode()).hexdigest()[:20] return self.dir / f"{h}.json" def get(self, case_id, fingerprint): p = self._key(case_id, fingerprint) return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None def put(self, case_id, fingerprint, result): self._key(case_id, fingerprint).write_text(json.dumps(result)) ``` Since the fingerprint (Day 35) changes when anything relevant changes, this is safe — and it typically cuts CI eval cost by 60–80% on PRs that touch unrelated code. ##### The runner ```python import time import numpy as np from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor def run_eval_suite(cases, system_fn, evaluator, fingerprint, cache=None, max_workers=8, price_in=0.0125, price_out=0.05): """Execute the suite, aggregate, and return a comparable result dict.""" def run_one(case): if cache: hit = cache.get(case.id, fingerprint) if hit: return hit t0 = time.perf_counter() try: result = system_fn(case.question) error = None except Exception as e: result, error = {"answer": "", "chunks": [], "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0}, str(e) latency = time.perf_counter() - t0 scored = evaluator.evaluate(case, result) record = { **scored, "latency_s": round(latency, 3), "cost_inr": round(result.get("tokens_in", 0) / 1000 * price_in + result.get("tokens_out", 0) / 1000 * price_out, 5), "error": error, } if cache and error is None: cache.put(case.id, fingerprint, record) return record with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool: records = list(pool.map(run_one, cases)) by_category = {} for cat in {r["category"] for r in records}: subset = [r for r in records if r["category"] == cat] by_category[cat] = round( sum(r["passed"] for r in subset) / len(subset), 4) latencies = [r["latency_s"] for r in records] return { "system_fingerprint": fingerprint, "n_cases": len(records), "n_passed": sum(r["passed"] for r in records), "overall_pass_rate": round(sum(r["passed"] for r in records) / len(records), 4), "by_category": by_category, "p50_latency": round(float(np.percentile(latencies, 50)), 3), "p95_latency": round(float(np.percentile(latencies, 95)), 3), "cost_per_query": round(float(np.mean([r["cost_inr"] for r in records])), 5), "errors": sum(1 for r in records if r["error"]), "failures": [{"case_id": r["case_id"], "category": r["category"], "failed_checks": r["failed_checks"]} for r in records if not r["passed"]], } ``` **`by_category` is what makes the gate meaningful.** An overall pass rate of 91% can hide unanswerable cases dropping from 100% to 60%, which is exactly the Pune failure. ##### Growing the eval set ```python def promote_production_failures(feedback_records, trace_client, eval_set_path, classifier, max_promote=20): """Turn production failures into permanent regression tests.""" promoted = [] for fb in feedback_records: if fb.rating != "down": continue trace = trace_client.get_trace(fb.trace_id) mode = classifier(trace) case = EvalCase( id=f"prod-{fb.trace_id[:8]}", category=mode, question=trace.input["question"], context="\n\n".join(c["text"] for c in trace.metadata["chunks"]), must_not_contain=_extract_bad_claims(trace.output, fb.reason), should_refuse=(mode == "content_not_in_corpus"), difficulty="hard", tags=["from_production", f"trace:{fb.trace_id}"], ) promoted.append(case) if len(promoted) >= max_promote: break _append_to_eval_set(eval_set_path, promoted) return {"promoted": len(promoted), "by_category": _count_by(promoted, "category")} ``` **An eval set built from production failures converges on what actually breaks.** After six months it is a far better predictor of real quality than anything you could have designed upfront — and every case in it is a bug that will never silently return. **Keep the set balanced.** Promoting only failures produces a set that is 90% hard cases, which makes the pass rate uninformative and the gate hypersensitive. Cap the hard fraction at around 40%. ##### The evaluation strategy document The assignment. A defensible structure: ```python EVALUATION_STRATEGY = { "offline": { "golden_set": { "size": 120, "composition": { "extraction": 0.25, "reasoning": 0.20, "unanswerable": 0.20, # highest-value category "multi_hop": 0.15, "edge_cases": 0.10, "adversarial": 0.10, }, "runtime_target_minutes": 4, "blocking": True, "run_on": "every PR touching app/, prompts/, config/", }, "full_suite": { "size": 600, "includes": ["golden set", "public benchmarks", "domain corpus", "all promoted production failures"], "runtime_minutes": 55, "blocking": False, "run_on": "nightly and pre-release", }, "metrics": { "rule_based": ["must_contain", "must_not_contain", "refusal_behaviour", "numbers_grounded", "retrieval_hit"], "ragas": ["faithfulness", "answer_relevancy", "context_precision", "context_recall"], "judge": ["correctness", "groundedness", "completeness", "conciseness"], "operational": ["p50_latency", "p95_latency", "cost_per_query"], }, }, "online": { "canary": {"stages": [0.01, 0.05, 0.15, 0.50, 1.00], "min_samples_per_stage": 500, "soak_minutes": 30, "auto_rollback_on": ["error_rate", "p95_latency", "refusal_rate", "thumbs_down_rate"]}, "continuous": {"quality_proxies": ["refusal_rate", "citation_count", "top_retrieval_score"], "explicit_feedback": "thumbs + reason", "implicit_signals": ["rephrase_rate", "copy_rate", "abandonment"]}, }, "regression_policy": { "zero_tolerance": ["unanswerable pass rate", "hallucination_guard", "refusal_behaviour"], "tolerances": {"overall_pass_rate": 0.02, "faithfulness": 0.03, "p95_latency": "+20%", "cost_per_query": "+15%"}, "baseline_update": "on merge to main after a passing gate", }, "judge_governance": { "model": "gpt-4o (different family from the generator)", "calibration": "50 human-labelled cases, Spearman >= 0.75", "recalibrate_when": ["judge model changes", "rubric changes", "quarterly"], }, "eval_set_maintenance": { "promote_from_production": "weekly triage, max 20 per week", "hard_case_cap": 0.40, "review_cadence": "quarterly — retire cases that never fail", }, } ``` ##### Common mistakes - **No blocking gate** — the Friday prompt change. - **No unanswerable cases**, so a lost refusal instruction is undetectable. - **Overall pass rate only**, hiding a category collapse. - **Non-zero tolerance on safety properties.** - **Judge uncalibrated**, or the same model family as the generator. - **Sequential judging in CI**, making the gate too slow to keep. - **No guardrail metrics**, shipping a quality win that tripled cost. - **Baseline updated automatically on failure**, which silently ratchets quality down. - **Eval set that only grows with hard cases**, making the pass rate uninformative. - **No caching**, so CI eval cost scales with PR count rather than with change. - **Never retiring cases** that have passed for a year and test nothing. - **Evaluating only the final answer for agents**, missing inefficient or unsafe trajectories. ##### Hands-on: make the gate block Your practical task builds an automated RAG evaluation pipeline with RAGAS and a golden dataset, run on every change. Keep it under five minutes — parallelise the judge calls, cache deterministic results, and cap the set at roughly 120 cases. Then deliberately break something (remove the refusal instruction, as in the Pune story) and confirm the gate catches it. A gate you have not seen block is a gate you do not know works. The mini project adds the eval gate to CI so it blocks merges on regression. Wire the PR comment — it is what makes the gate feel like help rather than obstruction. Set zero tolerance on your unanswerable and hallucination-guard categories, and reasonable tolerances elsewhere. Then open a PR with a deliberate regression and watch it fail with a readable explanation. The assignment writes an evaluation strategy covering offline, online, and regression testing. Structure it like the dictionary above but justify each choice in prose: why this golden-set composition, why these tolerances, why this judge model. Include the judge governance section — an evaluation strategy that does not say how the judge is calibrated and when it is revalidated is missing the part that makes the numbers trustworthy. ##### Key takeaways - **An evaluation you run manually is one you will skip.** The blocking CI gate is the artefact that actually prevents regressions. - **Include unanswerable cases with zero regression tolerance** — a lost refusal instruction looks like an improvement on every metric except hallucination rate. - **Run cheap rule checks before the LLM judge**, and report pass rates by category, because an overall number hides category collapse. - **RAGAS separates retrieval from generation failure** — read context recall against faithfulness before deciding what to fix. - **Grow the eval set from production failures**, cap the hard-case fraction, and recalibrate your judge whenever the model or rubric changes.
practical_task_reference: Build an automated RAG evaluation pipeline with RAGAS metrics and a golden dataset, run on every change.
mini_project_reference: Add an eval gate to a CI pipeline that blocks merges when quality metrics regress beyond a threshold.
assignment_reference: Design an evaluation strategy document covering offline, online, and regression testing for a GenAI product.
